title: Point of view / perspective Practice 2
description: 4 short texts - 8 focused point of view / perspective questions
subject: rla
passage:
TEXT A - Lost Key

I watched Arun search every pocket twice. He laughed when I offered to help, but because he kept glancing toward the locked office, I suspected he was more worried than he sounded.

TEXT B - River Project

Engineers say a new floodwall would protect several low streets. Environmental groups argue that restoring wetland space could reduce water levels while providing habitat.

TEXT C - Gallery Review

The critic praises the exhibition's dim lighting as intimate. A visitor quoted later says the same lighting makes labels difficult to read.

TEXT D - Lunch Policy

The principal supports a shorter lunch line because it gives students more time to eat. A cafeteria worker agrees with the goal but says the proposed layout could block access to storage.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the perspective or perspectives in this text?
questions.explanation: The narrator can observe Arun and make an inference but cannot know his private feeling with certainty.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: The narrator reports Arun’s worry as a direct statement from Arun.
options.whyWrong: “The narrator reports Arun’s worry as a direct statement from Arun.” conflicts with a detail stated in the passage.

options.text: Because the narrator uses first person, the narrator automatically knows Arun’s exact thoughts.
options.whyWrong: “Because the narrator uses first person, the narrator automatically knows Arun’s exact thoughts.” makes the text more certain or extreme than its wording supports.

options.text: The narrator can observe Arun and infer concern, but cannot know Arun’s private feeling with certainty.
The passage is told from Arun’s point of view even though another person says “I.”
options.whyWrong: “The passage is told from Arun’s point of view even though another person says “I.”” misstates whose perspective is presented or what that person emphasizes.

options.text: The point of view removes uncertainty by explaining why the key is missing.
options.whyWrong: The passage does not support “The point of view removes uncertainty by explaining why the key is missing..” This adds a claim the text never establishes.

options.whyWrong: “The perspective gives readers direct access to Arun’s thoughts but not the narrator’s.” misstates whose perspective is presented or what that person emphasizes.
